# Auth: email verification and password reset

Generated by `skies g auth:email`. Tokens are stored hashed and only leave the system in an email, so the cases in
`e2e/` layer a capturing `IEmailSender` over the booted app to read the token the real slice sent.

## Behavior

- `POST /account/verify-email/request` (authenticated) emails the caller a verification token valid for 24 hours.
- `POST /account/verify-email` consumes the token and marks the email verified.
- `POST /account/password-reset/request` emails a reset token valid for one hour to a registered address and
  answers the same way whether or not the address has an account.
- `POST /account/password-reset` consumes the token, sets the new password, and ends every existing session.
- `POST /account/register` with an address that already has an account answers as for a new one and mails the
  address's owner that someone tried to register it.

Before `skies proof run` or `record`, review each mode against the AVP catalog and add criteria or a reviewed
exemption. Generated code cannot make that applicability decision on behalf of the consuming app.

## Failure modes

- FM-1 A reset token from the email does not set the new password
- FM-2 A wrong reset token changes the password
- FM-3 A reset accepts a password shorter than the minimum
- FM-4 Sessions opened before a password reset survive it
- FM-5 Requesting a reset reveals whether an email is registered, or mails an unregistered address
- FM-6 The emailed verification token does not mark the email verified
- FM-7 A wrong verification token confirms the email, or consumes the real one
- FM-8 Registering a taken email mails nothing to its owner
- FM-9 A reset or verification request that leaves a field out of its body fails as a server error, or mails anyone

## Out of scope

- Delivery: the dev `ConsoleEmailSender` prints the message. A real provider is an `IEmailSender` the app registers.
- The throttle on requesting a token: the Account module's credential rate limit, proven with the auth spec.
